topic: Side point: Arlong's per-head prices show Bell-mere's 100,000 exactly covered Nami and Nojiko, not herself
title: Bell-mere's Price Math Nobody Noticed In Arlong Park
description: Bell-mere's coins in One Piece Arlong Park, explained: the per-head prices show exactly who she paid for. A small detail from chapters 77 to 79 that changes how Nami learned to carry every cost alone. Did she choose, or was she out of options?
comment: Did Bell-mere choose Nami and Nojiko over herself, or was she simply out of options?

lines.text: Nobody noticed what Bell-mere's coins actually bought in chapter 78.

shot.fallback: mother with two little girls facing a shark fishman

lines.text: Arlong names his price for Cocoyasi Village. One hundred thousand per adult, fifty thousand per child.
Bell-mere has exactly one hundred thousand to her name.

shot.fallback: woman counting a small pile of coins

lines.text: Now do the math. Two girls at fifty thousand each is one hundred thousand.
She never paid for herself. She paid for Nami and Nojiko, and Arlong took the deal.

shot.fallback: mother facing a fishman with coins in hand

lines.text: Arlong still takes Nami, because she can draw maps, so the coins never bought her freedom.

shot.fallback: fishman handing a girl a map

lines.text: Later, at Bell-mere's grave, she tells Nojiko she struck a deal to buy the village back.

shot.fallback: girl at a grave under a tangerine tree

lines.text: The price is one hundred million berries. Chapter 79.
People say Bell-mere just ran out of money. Fair, but she picked whose price to cover.
And Nami learned the lesson: love means paying the whole bill and telling nobody.

shot.fallback: girl alone with a map and coins

lines.text: So why does Oda's newest chapter feel like it was written about her?
Because the detail nobody noticed is what Bell-mere's coins actually bought.

shot.fallback: two girls beside a coin pile

self_check.hook: Line 1 names Bell-mere's coins and the detail nobody noticed.
self_check.loop: Last line leads back into line 1.
